messages:
ellie: quick dump from today's kernel-selector + batching sweep. saw a small-but-noticeable P95 bump on L4 when sequences > 1k tokens hit the slow attention fallback. thinking we should tighten max_tokens_per_batch for the smaller cards and relax for A100/H100.

raj: can you paste the numbers? how big is the bump?

ellie: P50 stays same, P95 on L4 goes from ~120ms -> ~230ms on mixed workloads (avg seq len 900). throughput drops ~18% under 90% util. KV cache hit-rate looks okay (~83%) but fragmentation + kernel-switch seems to trigger serialization.

chen: do you have the kernel-selector logs? I want to see why it fell back.

ellie: yes, attached snippet below from perf run (simplified):
```
[kernel-select] model: llama-13b, seq: 1024, kv_chunks: 4
selected_kernel: fwd_attn_fast (A100/H100 path)
fallback_kernel: fwd_attn_generic (L4 path)
reason: tile_size_mismatch -> increased memory pressure -> fallback
latency: 230ms (fallback) vs 115ms (fast)
```

lina: hmm. sounds like our tile sizing logic picks a kernel that doesn't play well when combined with KV cache fragments. maybe the selector threshold is too aggressive for L4 memory layout.

sophia: proposal: use per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch caps to keep L4/T4/A10 in the fast-kernel regime. also limit max_batch_size when seqs > 512 to avoid memory spikes that force fallback.

mike: +1 to caps. what are we proposing numerically?

ellie: draft values from the sweep (these are conservative starting points):

```
# proposed max_tokens_per_batch
A10: 1536  # workloads with short-medium seqs still fine
T4: 1024  # keep below heavy kernel fallback
L4: 768   # avoid long-seq fallback observed above
A100: 8192 # increase to favor throughput
H100: 12288# max throughput for batch packing
```
ellie: additionally: adjust queue policy so that requests with seq > 768 are preferentially routed to A100/H100 pools when available, otherwise cap their tokens in L4/T4 to 512.

raj: can we simulate the effects? we should measure tail latency and token/s.

perf-bot: ran queued sim for these caps on the mixed workload profile:
- L4: throughput -12%, P95 +90ms (improved vs unconstrained)
- T4: throughput -8%, P95 +60ms
- A100: throughput +22% (pack more tokens), P95 -15ms
- H100: throughput +28%, P95 -20ms
(simulation config: 10k requests, seq dist mean=640, kv-hit=0.82)

chen: those sim results look promising. what about memory OOM risk?

ellie: memory headroom improved on smaller cards because we avoid packing large seqs into single batch. we still saw occasional OOM on T4 when we allowed 1024 tokens AND batch_size=64; so we should keep batch_size cap 32 for T4 when seqs > 512.

lina: can we add a fallback policy: if kernel-selector would fallback to slow kernel, mark the request with a "defer_to_high_mem" tag and try overflow routing?

ops-bot: added runbook stub: /runbooks/batching/fallback-routing (ops only).

mike: next steps: 1) implement per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch config knobs, 2) add queue routing rule for seq>768, 3) run canary on staging with 5% traffic to validate P95.

ellie: plan sounds good. I'll file the config PR and schedule the canary. @raj @chen can you help run a short A/B with the old vs new selector? aim for start tomorrow morning.

raj: happy to. I'll kick off the sim today and post logs.

sophia: one more ask — add a quick telemetry gauge for "kernel_fallback_rate_by_gpu" so we can see if the caps actually reduce fallbacks.

ellie: yep adding that to the PR. thanks everyone :rocket:

perf-bot: note: keep an eye on KV cache eviction churn when you change packing — more small batches can increase eviction frequency for long-lived sessions.

ellie: noted, we'll monitor kv-eviction-rate during canary.

mike: :thumbsup:
